title: Interactive statusflow + customer choiceboard (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This draft is an "interactive statusflow" and customer choiceboard we can publish as a status page follow-up + customer email for incidents that cause progressive inference quality regressions or intermittent latency. The goal is twofold: 1) give customers clear, actionable choices with tradeoffs (fastest recovery vs. highest data fidelity) and 2) provide a predictable sequence of public status updates they can subscribe to and automate against.

TL;DR (for status page header):
We experienced intermittent inference quality regressions impacting a subset of tenant requests in our hosted EU region. Short-term mitigations are in place; you have three recovery choices below (automatic fallthrough, manual replay opt-in, or conservative rollback). We're continuing verification and will publish minute-by-minute progress updates here.

What happened (plain language):
On 2026-11-12 at ~03:40 UTC, a deployment step triggered a model routing mismatch between two model variants used for low-latency fallbacks. This caused inconsistent tokenization/response post-processing for a subset of in-flight sessions, leading to truncated or semantically-shifted outputs for approximately 0.7% of requests across EU region between 03:40 and 04:20 UTC. No customer data was exfiltrated.

Scope & impact (concise):
- Affected customers: subset of hosted API tenants using model routing that includes the v2f fallback path (catalog label: open-v2f-lowlatency).
- User visible: truncated/odd completions and occasional semantic drift.
- Magnitude: ~0.7% of requests in EU region during the window (internal metric).
- Duration: incident window ~40 minutes; mitigations applied at 04:05 UTC; full remediation completed 04:22 UTC.

What we did (customer-forward):
- Immediately paused rollouts of the routing change and disabled the v2f fallback path at 04:05 UTC.
- Re-routed in-flight sessions to the stable variant; enabled prefix-KV replay where feasible.
- Began automated verification against a representative prompt set and replayed logs to measure divergence.
- Notified impacted customers via tenant-notifications API and this status page.

Customer choices (choiceboard):
We know different customers have different risk tolerances. Below are three supported recovery options you can select in your tenant portal or via the API. Each includes the expected outcome, steps we will take, and suggested customer validation checks. Choose by 2026-11-18 23:59 UTC for bulk opt-ins; individual replay can be requested anytime but may take longer.

Option A — Automatic fallthrough (default; no action required)
- What we do: Keep the stable variant enabled (what we already did). We will not replay impacted requests unless you opt-in.
- Expected outcome: No further user-visible regression; no guaranteed restoration of affected outputs.
- Best for: customers prioritizing availability and lowest operational friction.
- Customer validation: Spot-check recent examples; ingest as-is if you do not require identical replays.

Option B — Replay opt-in (recommended for deterministic outputs)
- What we do: With your consent, we will run an automated replay pipeline for impacted request IDs and produce regenerated outputs using the stable variant. We will surface a proof package (request IDs, input prompts, resulting outputs, and checksum) so you can verify.
- Expected outcome: Most requests will be re-generated to match the pre-incident expected behavior; some non-deterministic outputs may still differ (we'll flag these).
- Best for: customers who need output fidelity (search index updates, billing-sensitive flows, support transcripts).
- Customer validation: Use provided checksums and sample diff tool; run your regression test suite against the replay results.

Option C — Conservative rollback + snapshot (recommended for high-integrity workloads)
- What we do: For a limited window you can request a conservative rollback to a pinned model revision and request we apply a snapshot-based replay with stricter determinism (longer runtime, higher cost). This is limited to tenants with active dedicated contracts or private deployments; hosted tenants may request an exception.
- Expected outcome: Highest chance of matching pre-incident outputs, at the cost of delayed availability for replay and higher compute.
- Best for: regulated workloads where record fidelity is required.
- Customer validation: We will provide end-to-end evidence including model revision, execution logs, and reproducibility checksum.

How to choose / opt-in steps:
- Tenant portal: Settings > Incident Recovery > "Choose recovery option" and select A/B/C.
- API: POST /v1/tenant/{id}/recovery-choice body {"choice": "replay"} (example in tenant portal).
- If you do nothing: Option A remains in effect.

Verification and evidence we will provide:
- For replayed requests we will publish: request_id, original input, new output, execution-time, model-revision, and SHA256 checksum.
- We will also publish an aggregated verification report: divergence rate, sample diffs, and confidence tag (deterministic | probabilistic).

Suggested status page update cadence (minute-level examples):
- 04:10 UTC — "Mitigations applied: v2f fallback disabled for EU; routing paused. Initial checks show reduction in anomalous completions."
- 04:22 UTC — "Full remediation: routing corrected, verification started. Affected request count: ~0.7% of EU requests."
- Publish subsequent updates every 20–60 minutes during verification, then a final summary once replay decisions complete.

Sample short customer-facing update for status page (one-line):
- "We have mitigated the service regression in EU and are offering replay and rollback options for impacted requests — choose via Tenant Portal or API. See guidance for tradeoffs."

Sample email template (subject + short body):
Subject: Action available — Redwood Inference incident recovery options (EU, 2026-11-12)
Body: Hello — We identified an EU-region inference regression on 2026-11-12 that may have affected a subset of your requests. We have stabilized service. You can choose how we handle affected requests in the Tenant Portal (Options: keep as-is, automated replay, conservative rollback). If you want replay help or a digest of affected request IDs, reply to this message or open a support ticket.

Operational checklist for CS agents (bullet points):
- Confirm tenant subscription tier and whether dedicated/private exception applies.
- If tenant requests replay: collect consent, expected validation timeframe, and any PII handling constraints.
- Trigger replay queue with tenant id; monitor progress and follow verification steps.
- Deliver proof package to tenant and wait for confirmation before closing.
- If rollback requested: coordinate with SRE/serving-runtime for schedule and cost estimate.

Internal risks & open questions (notes for cross-team):
- Edge case: sessions that spanned the injection point and had partial KV cache mismatch — replays may behave nondeterministically. We need an explicit flag in replay tooling to mark "best-effort" vs "strict" replay.
- Compliance: replay for tenants with restricted data needs KMS/HSM audit; CS must confirm and record consent.
- Billing: replay compute will be billed as per sentry pricing unless we offer credits; decide commercial approach for enterprise customers.

Follow-up timeline (owner: Customer Success lead + SRE):
- 2026-11-17: Publish choiceboard and API opt-ins (this doc).
- 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-22: Bulk opt-in window for tenants to choose Option B or C.
- 2026-11-23 to 2026-12-03: Replay window for bulk opt-ins (staggered based on queue).
- 2026-12-10: Close incident and publish final customer-facing postmortem with verification artifacts.

Acceptance criteria for final postmortem (what customers will expect):
- Clear root cause summary and a timeline.
- Exact list of affected tenants and request counts (per-tenant aggregate).
- Delivered replay proof packages for opt-ins.
- Action items and planned mitigations to prevent recurrence.

Appendix: quick FAQ (customer-friendly)
Q: Will replay change my billing?
A: Replay compute is billable under normal rules; for enterprise tenants we may offer credits on a case-by-case basis — CS will surface options during opt-in.

Q: I need guaranteed identical outputs — which option is best?
A: Choose Option C (conservative rollback + snapshot). Note this may take longer and has compute cost.

Q: How long until I see replay results?
A: Typical replay latency per-tenant depends on queue position and request volume; small tenants often see results within 24–72 hours in the bulk window.

Internal next steps (immediate):
- CS: review copy and voice, prepare tenant portal UI text, and draft API examples. (owner: Priya)
- SRE/Serving Runtime: add strict/best-effort replay flag and ETA signal in replay API. (owner: Liam)
- Product: coordinate billing/credits guidance and finalize commercial policy. (owner: Marcus)

Notes: This draft aims for clarity and actionable choices rather than prescriptive remediation. Request feedback from SRE and product by 2026-11-18 EOD so we can publish a status page entry and enable API opt-ins on 2026-11-19 morning UTC.
